narrative.text: Objective & Process Outline
Objective: To grow recombinant Saccharomyces cerevisiae in optimum sterile fed batch conditions, which promote the growth and high yield of the desired product.
Process outline: The process consists of a glycerol stock, pre-seed culture, seed culture, fermentation (Batch phase and Fed batch phase), and harvest.
COMPAN Strain: STRAIN_X
Equipment: , Total Volume: 3.7 L, Working Volume 2.5L-3L. BIOREACTOR_A BIOREACTOR_A
Spectrophotometer- Hitachi 1900U.
pH meter- Hanna Benchtop PH/MV Meter.
A. Salt solution composition:
B. Carbon source composition:
Batch medium composition:
Seed Culture: Prepared seed culture by inoculating 5% (1mL) glycerol stock into 20ml of DELFT medium in standard 100ml shake flask and incubated at 30°C (220rpm) for overnight.
Inoculated the overnight seed culture into 200ml of DELFT medium to an OD600 of 0.5 in a standard conical flask (1000 ml) and incubated the culture at 30°C at 220rpm for overnight.
Inoculated the bioreactor with 100mL of the prepared seed inoculum (Initial batch volume was 1500mL).
o Temperature: 30°C.
o pH: 5.5 (maintained using 25% Ammonia or ortho phosphoric acid 85% for acid/base control).
o Agitation: 600 rpm.
o Aeration: 1 vvm (volume of air per volume of medium per minute).
o Dissolved Oxygen (DO): Calibrated to 100% before inoculation and monitored continuously.
Allowed the batch phase to proceed without feeding.
Monitored OD600, pH, DO, and temperature regularly.
Samples taken periodically to measure glucose concentration, biomass, and byproducts (e.g., ethanol).
Fed-Batch Phase: Started the fed-batch phase when the carbon source (glucose) was nearly depleted (typically when OD600 reaches ~20-25 or DO Spike).
Started feeding at a rate of 5 mL/L/h.
Gradually increase the feeding rate to 15 mL/L/h based on the following criteria.
Maintained DO above 20% saturation (adjust agitation needed).
Avoided glucose accumulation (monitored glucose concentration periodically).
Monitored OD600 and adjusted feeding to maintain growth.
Batch closure: The batch was terminated at 82 h (planned 96 h) due to onset of cell death and the appearance of white cells during centrifugation.
During the initial batch phase, exponential growth was observed as the yeast utilized the available nutrients in the batch medium.
The fed-batch phase allowed for sustained growth and prevented substrate depletion.
The gradual increase in feed rate ensured that glucose concentrations remained below inhibitory levels, minimizing the risk of overflow metabolism.
The addition of yeast extract supported protein synthesis and metabolic activity, leading to the production of desired metabolites.
